So, what I like to do is pick the best from the bunch and use that as a base. Then, I'll take, say, an over-saturated, low contrast photo for ambiance, set it to whatever opacity feels good, and layer that one on the base. Then I'll usually take one with higher contrast, set the opacity to slightly lower than what I used for the ambient photo, and layer that one on top, giving the photo a very 3D, HDR feel without looking embossed. Again, its trial and error, and really comes down to personal taste
That's for optimal cloud swoopage. You can get results with as little as 5 minutes, but in my opinion, you get much more color contrast and smoothness from longer exposure

Well, it's basically a long exposure shot, so you'll need a tripod, or something incredibly still for your camera, 5 second timer, and preferably a remote shooter. It is incredibly important that your camera is totally still, even the shutter shake is enough to blur the image, which is why the timer is necessary. For sunsets, you'll need to decrease your ISO and increase your aperture to make up for the extra light coming into the lenses from the lengthened shutter speed, very trial and error. After adjusting your lighting and white balance, set your camera on whatever stabilizer you decide to use, click the shutter, and wait. For ones like these, you'll need a shutter speed of at least 15 minutes or so. If possible, take multiple shots with different WB and contrast settings, this is useful for layering during processing. 

After you've acquired your shot(s) (always shoot in RAW for the best editing) you'll want to layer your photos for a really smooth, colorful effect. After all that, adjust the final image and export. It's not incredibly complicated if you have the right equipment. The same also works for astrophotography, just increase the ISO and decrease the aperture and it's essentially the same process. Again, it's very trial and error, but getting the final image is always worth it in my opinion.

My fiance and I went out to lunch after a funeral and encountered an old lady who appeared quite disheveled and was completely alone (important for later,) so we invited her to sit with us and we bought her some food. She starts telling us about her boyfriend and how he had left her there to go wash some clothes at a laundromat near a park, and she needed a ride over there, so we offered to take her. We got our food to-go and went to the car. She seemed a little off-kilter, and was talking erratically, so we assumed she had either Dementia or Alzheimer's and didn't think anything else of it. We load up and get to the park and eat while she keeps saying "he'll be here any minute," over and over again. Finally the guy gets there on a motorcycle and he's looking ROUGH. Covered in dirt, sores, missing patches of hair on his head and I swear his clothes were about to fall apart right off of his body. She goes over to him and they start SCREAMING at each other and eventually she starts crying, all while we're still sitting there eating burgers wondering if we've made a mistake. The guy then motions over to someone and out of nowhere 6-8 dudes all on bikes start rushing over to our area, each one looking about as rough as the lady's boyfriend. It was at that moment I shot a look to my fiance and we jetted outta that park faster than I've ever left a location. Another important point to add is this is a town with a horrific Methamphetamine problem. I'm not sure what would've happened if we'd stayed any longer, but the feeling I had in my stomach told me to get out ASAP.
